_note: Luồng 03 — Hoá đơn thanh toán / đề nghị hoàn ứng. Each case gives: POST /vouchers (voucherType=expense_claim), then PATCH /vouchers/{{voucherId}}/apply-extraction with an extractedFields body (snake_case keys — this blob follows the extraction-skill schema, agent/skills/voucher-universal-extractor/SKILL.md, not the C# camelCase API DTOs), then POST /vouchers/{{voucherId}}/expense-claim-result/propose. Approval-chain calls (department-review/accounting-review/apply-expense) use the exact routes added for R14 (gateway/src/Aiq.Gateway/Endpoints/VoucherEndpoints.cs). All category names below must exist in the expense_policies loaded from master_data.json for the case to behave as documented. VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-15) against a freshly-bootstrapped isolated instance: EXP-001's full propose -> tax-verification-gate -> 3-stage-approval -> journal-proposal chain reproduced every expected number exactly. IMPORTANT (found during that verification): the 3-stage chain requires 4 DISTINCT people in total — whoever creates/proposes the voucher can NEVER perform department-review, accounting-review, OR apply-expense on it (self-approval is blocked with 403 at every one of those 3 calls, not just the final one) — always use an admin account that did not create the voucher for all 3 stages, and a different admin for each of the 3 stages.

approvalChain: apply-expense (Admin C, distinct from A and B)

expected.gateBeforeFinalApproval: apply-expense returns 409 tax_verification_required until POST /vouchers/{{voucherId}}/tax-verification/confirm is called (a real invoice_no is present).

expected.note: meal category has no vendor_mst/invoice_no in this line — CIT non-deductible would apply if requiresTaxVerification mattered here, but the policy for 'meal' does not require a receipt either way; approvedAmount is fully reimbursable.

The current policy engine applies a FLAT per_item cap (department_expense_policies.limit_amount) regardless of the limit_unit label ('per_night' is descriptive only — there is no night-count/quantity field on an expense item to multiply by). With NV-001's rank (Chuyên viên) capped at 1,500,000 per item, a 3,000,000 claim is cut to exactly 1,500,000, not the business document's illustrative 2,400,000 (which implies a 2-night multiplier the code does not currently implement) — see BUSINESS_SAMPLE_TEST_MATRIX.md for this discrepancy note.
expected.rankComparison: The SAME line submitted for NV-002 (Trưởng phòng, limit 2,500,000) would cap to 2,500,000 instead — see master_data.json expense_policies.

cases.label: Wrong approval-stage attempt (skip / repeat-actor, must be blocked)
steps: 1. Admin B (not the creator) calls POST /accounting-review directly, skipping department-review -> expect 409 (still review_status='proposed').
2. Admin B calls POST /apply-expense directly -> expect 409 (still 'proposed', needs 'accounting_reviewed').
3. Admin B calls POST /department-review -> expect 200, review_status becomes 'dept_reviewed'.
4. Admin B (SAME actor as step 3) calls POST /accounting-review -> expect 409 (separation of duties: must be a different admin).
5. Admin C calls POST /accounting-review -> expect 200, review_status becomes 'accounting_reviewed'.
6. Admin B or Admin C calls POST /apply-expense -> expect 409 (must be a THIRD distinct admin).
7. Admin D calls POST /apply-expense -> expect 200, review_status becomes 'confirmed'.

expected.sequenceEnforced: Exactly as in gateway/tests-adjacent E2E test_expense_payment_e2e.sh §15 — 3 distinct actors required, never the creator, no skipping, no repeat-actor.
